duties.duty: ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C001 (partial): Hypotheses and source variant are not supplied (failure condition: unstated assumption). def:p15-filtration-martingale (body 18-26) defines adaptedness but never requires it. A martingale is therefore any real process with integrable terms and E(X_{n+1}|F_n)=X_n, and sub/supermartingales swap the identity for an inequality. The held source's definition (Durrett PTE5 p. 217) has three conditions, and condition (ii), 'X_n adapted to F_n', is dropped. For sub- and supermartingales the inequality does not imply adaptedness. The handbook's own proofs still rely on it: annex 77 says 'The case n=m follows from adaptedness', annex 91 says 'adaptedness was explicitly assumed', and annex 35/104/124/150/412/559/586/734 check adaptedness. The optional-stopping chapter on the same route states the convention outright (optional-stopping-and-random-walks.tex 12-13). Concrete case: take F_n trivial, X_0=-2-U and X_n=-1 for n>=1. This meets the definition as written, but the n=m case of thm:p15-martingale-conditioning fails.
